Ask a decision model typed questions

decide.Rd

Sends each input (a text, an image or both) with the questions to one model and returns, for each input, the answer and a probability for each allowed answer.

Usage

decide(
  decider,
  questions,
  text = NULL,
  image = NULL,
  references = NULL,
  max_size = 768,
  upscale = FALSE,
  crop = "none",
  max_active = 10,
  rpm = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  ignore_hash = FALSE
)

Arguments

decider

A decider from decider_typesafe(), decider_openai(), decider_foundry(), decider_openrouter() or decider_systemone(); or a setup from decision_setup() or read_setup(). A setup gives the decider, the questions, the prepared references, the image settings and a calibrator. With a setup, give the inputs by name (text = , image = ), and leave out questions, references, max_size, upscale and crop: they stop decide() with an error.

questions

One question from question_noul(), question_choice() or question_score(), or a named list of questions. The names are the question names of the request, kept exactly. With two or more questions, the names, cleaned as the answer names are, are the prefixes of the output columns; two names that give the same prefix are refused. One question without a name is sent as question.

text

A character vector with one text per input, or NULL.

image

A character vector of file paths or URLs, a list of magick images, or a magick vector of several images (for example magick::image_read(paths)), with one image per input; or NULL. A file with several frames (GIF, TIFF, PDF) gives its first frame. With text, element i of text and element i of image make input i.

references

Reference images for the answers, or NULL: a named list in which each name is an allowed answer of the question and each element holds the images of that answer (paths, URLs or magick images). This release takes references with one question only.

max_size

The longest side of each image in pixels after the resize (one number of 1 or more), or NULL to keep the size. The default is 768.

upscale

TRUE enlarges an image that is smaller than max_size. FALSE (the default) never enlarges.

crop

"none" (the default), "center", a box c(x, y, width, height) in pixels, or a function that takes a magick image and returns a box. max_size, upscale and crop apply to the inputs and to the references.

max_active

The largest number of requests in progress at the same time. The default is 10.

rpm

The largest number of requests per minute, or NULL (the default) for no limit. The requests then go out evenly, one each 60 / rpm seconds.

path

NULL (the default), or the path of a JSON file that keeps the finished answers, so that a long run that stops can continue without paying twice for an input (as ellmer::batch_chat() does). The folder must exist. The inputs that are not in the file go out in chunks of 4 * max_active, and decide() adds the answers of each chunk to the file. A new call with the same path sends only the inputs that are not in the file and returns all rows, in the order of the inputs. Rows with an .error are not written, so a new call sends them again. With path, identical inputs are sent once.

The file holds a hash of the run and, for each finished input (keyed by a hash of the prepared text and image), its answers with their probabilities, .model, .input_tokens, .cost and .seconds. It holds no key and no input. The hash covers the provider, the server URL, the model, the request format, the image format, the questions (instructions, answers and descriptions), the prepared reference images and the image settings; a crop function enters through its body.

The keys and the hash of the run come from rlang::hash(), and both cover prepared JPEG bytes (of the inputs, and of the references). Another version of ImageMagick (the library under magick) can give other JPEG bytes for the same image, and another version of rlang can give other hashes. So a path file continues a run on the computer that wrote it, with the same versions of ImageMagick and rlang. Elsewhere, the hash of the run can differ, or the inputs are sent again.

With a setup that holds a calibrator, the file keeps the answers before calibration, and the hash does not cover the calibrator: decide() applies the calibrator after it reads the file. So a new call with a refitted calibrator, or with none, reuses the answers of the file.

A file that is not a path file of decide() (for example a setup file of write_setup()) stops the call before any request, also with ignore_hash = TRUE, so decide() never replaces it.

ignore_hash

FALSE (the default) stops before any request when the hash in the path file differs from the hash of the run, that is, when the model, the questions, the references or the image settings changed. TRUE keeps the answers of the file with a warning and sends only the other inputs. The file gets the new hash when decide() adds answers to it; when the file holds every input, it does not change. Use TRUE only when you know that the change does not change the answers, for example the same model on a new server URL.

Value

A tibble with one row per input, in the order of the inputs:

  • For one question: .pred_class, a factor whose levels are the allowed answers, kept exactly (for example "not sure"); .pred_<answer>, the probability of each allowed answer; and .score for a score question. The probability columns have syntactic names: the answer cleaned as janitor::make_clean_names(case = "none") cleans it (ASCII letters, digits and _; X before a leading digit). For example, "not sure" gives .pred_not_sure, "late / lost" gives .pred_late_lost and "50%" gives .pred_X50_percent. probably and yardstick read these columns.

  • For two or more questions: the same columns with the cleaned question name and _ as a prefix, for example quality_.pred_class.

  • .model: the model that the provider reports, or the model of the decider when the response has none.

  • .input_tokens: the input tokens that the provider reports.

  • .cost: the cost that the provider reports, or NA.

  • .seconds: the time of the response.

  • .error: NA, or the reason why the answers of the row are NA.

The attribute requests of the tibble is the number of requests that this call sent (0 when a path file holds all the answers). A second try after HTTP 429 or 503 counts as a request.

With a setup that holds a calibrator, the calibrated probabilities of probably::cal_apply() replace the .pred_<answer> columns, and .pred_class is the answer with the highest calibrated probability (its levels stay the allowed answers). .score stays as the model gave it. The rows with an .error stay NA.

Details

One request goes out per input, in parallel (httr2::req_perform_parallel()), with at most max_active requests at a time and at most rpm requests per minute. Set rpm to the rate limit of your account: with no rpm, the first requests go out at full speed, and a provider with a rate limit then refuses some of them with HTTP 429.

Each request waits at most 300 seconds (5 minutes) for its response (httr2::req_timeout()). A request that takes longer gets a row error, so a server that stops responding does not hold the call. With path, a new call sends that input again.

A request that gets HTTP 429 or 503 is sent one more time, as the default retry policy of httr2 does (two tries, D170). decide() sends all such requests again together, after the longest wait that their Retry-After headers ask for (1 second without the header, at most 60 seconds). A second failure stays as a row error. So a call never waits long for a server that keeps refusing.

An interrupt (Esc) keeps the rows that are done. After an interrupt while the requests are out, nothing is sent again, and each request that did not finish gets a row error. An interrupt during the wait before the second tries skips them; their rows get the error "Interrupted before a retry." With path, an interrupt also stops the chunks: the file keeps every finished answer, the inputs that were not sent get the row error of a request that did not finish, and a new call sends only the rest. Each write goes to a temporary file in the same folder first, which then replaces the file, so a crash during a write leaves the previous file whole. When the file cannot be replaced (for example, while a sync program holds it), decide() tries again twice, and warns at the end with the number of finished answers that the file does not hold.

No row is lost. A row has NA answers and a message in .error when the call fails (the message holds the error text of the provider word for word, the model name and the size of the request in bytes), when the response cannot be read, when an answer is not an allowed answer or is missing, when the probability of an allowed answer is missing, or when the score of a score question is not one number or its probabilities are all zero. With path, a new call sends such a row again. A row with an answered call keeps its .input_tokens and .cost. A model, input_tokens or cost field that is not one value gives the model of the decider or NA.

Because .error keeps the text of the provider word for word, it can hold a part of the key: OpenAI answers a wrong key with HTTP 401 and a text that shows the last four characters of the key. Do not share the .error texts of a call with a wrong key.

decide() reads the key and checks the input type of the model before any request. For a provider with a key (all deciders except decider_systemone()), it stops unless the key is one non-empty string; the message does not show the key. For a setup with a calibrator, it also checks before any request that probably and the packages of the calibrator (for example mgcv) are installed. It prepares each reference image once per call (a setup holds its references prepared) and each input image once. With decider_systemone(image_format = "images"), it writes the images with three color channels.

Each image goes out as a JPEG, which has no transparency. So each pixel keeps its color and loses its transparency, and transparent areas often become black (a transparent pixel usually holds black, as "transparent" does in magick).

SystemOne links reference images to the answers of choice and noul questions. A SystemOne score question has no place for them: they are sent, but not linked to a level. OpenAI puts them in the instructions of the question, and the image-list format names them in the state text.

.cost holds only a cost that the provider reports (OpenRouter does). When no row has a cost, decide() prints one message that says so.

.seconds is the total time of the response as httr2::resp_timing() gives it; for a request that was sent again, it is the time of the second try. It is NA when no response arrived.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
refund <- question_noul("Does the message ask for a refund?")
decide(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), refund, text = c(
  "Please refund the second charge.",
  "Where is my parcel?"
))

quality <- question_choice("Inspect `inspection_image` for a defect.", c(
  normal = "A clean surface.", defective = "A dark streak."
))
decide(
  decider_openai(), list(quality = quality),
  image = c("part-1.jpg", "part-2.jpg"),
  references = list(normal = "good.jpg", defective = "streak.jpg")
)

# A setup holds the decider, the questions and the references
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), list(refund = refund))
decide(setup, text = "Please refund the second charge.")
} # }
